advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Constrain the reaper's walk to the root's own filesystem (compare st_dev against the /var/tmp device, prune cross-device dirs) so it matches `du -sx` and never deletes across a mount.
evidence: infra/scripts/vartmp-cap.sh:294: `for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(path, followlinks=False):` — followlinks=False guards symlinks but not mount crossings

infra/scripts/vartmp-cap.sh:257: `It sums APPARENT file sizes, while observability.sh sizes the same tree with \`du -sx\`` — asserts same tree, but du -sx stays on one filesystem while os.walk does not
infra/scripts/observability.sh:749: `var_tmp_bytes="$(bounded "$VAR_TMP_DU_TIMEOUT" du -sx --block-size=1 "$VAR_TMP_DIR" ...` — metric uses -x (one filesystem)

ABSENCE: candidates()/measure() never call os.stat().st_dev nor compare device ids to the root's, so a mounted subtree (the rejected bind-mount scenario, or any future mount under /var/tmp) is walked and rmtree'd
advisory.finding: The reaper's Python pass sizes and deletes with os.walk/os.listdir and no filesystem-boundary guard, but observability.sh sizes the same tree with `du -sx` (single-filesystem) and the reaper's own comment claims it measures 'the same tree'. If any filesystem is mounted beneath /var/tmp, the reaper crosses the mount — sizing and DELETING files the metric excludes with -x.
scenarios: A future or accidental mount under /var/tmp (e.g. the bind-mount alternative the ADR contemplated) leaves the reaper deleting data on the other volume while var_tmp_used_percent excludes those bytes, so the metric reads under budget yet the reaper is destroying unrelated data.
Under-budget metric but reaper still evicts because its cross-mount total exceeds the cap.
advisory.suggested_fix: In measure()/os.walk, capture the root's st_dev via os.lstat(root).st_dev and prune dirnames whose st_dev differs (and skip files on other devices), mirroring du -sx.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Have apply_quota propagate a non-zero result (or clearly re-assert enforcement) when the project/limit commands fail after accounting is ON, so --install does not report success on a failed limit.
evidence: infra/scripts/vartmp-cap.sh (apply_quota): `xfs_quota -x -c "limit -p bhard=... 2>/dev/null || warn "could not set ..."` — failure only warns, no non-zero propagation
report_state() re-checks quota_enforced independently, so the published var_tmp_hard_quota_in_effect stays honest — but the install command's own exit status does not reflect the failed limit
advisory.finding: apply_quota() downgrades every xfs_quota failure to a warn and returns 0, so `--install` reports success even when the `project -s` or `limit -p bhard` commands fail after accounting is ON — the box can believe a hard ceiling was applied when none was set.
scenarios: Operator has rebooted with rootflags=pquota (accounting ON) and runs --install; the limit command fails (e.g. permission, project-id collision) but install exits 0 and only a warn is emitted.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a defensive guard in the reaper so it refuses to run unless VAR_TMP_DIR is an absolute path under /var (and not '/'), before any rmtree/unlink.
evidence: infra/scripts/vartmp-cap.sh:270 `root, cap, min_age, descend, keep = sys.argv[1:6]`
infra/scripts/vartmp-cap.sh:352 `if os.path.isdir(path) and not os.path.islink(path):` then `shutil.rmtree(path, ignore_errors=False)`
VAR_TMP_DIR is env-overridable: `VAR_TMP_DIR="${VAR_TMP_DIR:-/var/tmp}"` and consumed by the reap python with no assertion that it equals a whitelisted path
advisory.finding: The oldest-first reaper runs as root from a systemd unit and performs shutil.rmtree()/os.unlink() on the contents of VAR_TMP_DIR with no validation that VAR_TMP_DIR actually resolves to /var/tmp (or is non-empty / not '/'). A misconfigured VAR_TMP_DIR (env override, eval of --print-env, or a future edit) would point a root-privileged recursive delete at an arbitrary directory. The default is safe and the installed unit passes no env, but there is no defensive floor for a destructive operation.
scenarios: An operator or a deploy exports VAR_TMP_DIR to a wrong value; the root-running reaper deletes top-level entries of that directory to a low-water mark.
advisory.suggested_fix: In the REAP python, assert `os.path.realpath(root)` starts with '/var/tmp' (or reject root in {'', '/', '/var', '/tmp'}) and SystemExit(0) with a stderr warning otherwise.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make apply_quota idempotent by skipping `project -s` / `limit` when the project id and bhard are already set to the intended values.
evidence: infra/scripts/vartmp-cap.sh:396 `xfs_quota -x -c "project -s -p ${VAR_TMP_DIR} ${VAR_TMP_PROJECT_ID}" "$VAR_TMP_QUOTA_FS"`
infra/scripts/compose-up.sh:99 `if ! bash "${SCRIPT_DIR}/vartmp-cap.sh" --install; then` (runs on every deploy)
apply_quota is called unconditionally at the end of --install when quota_accounting_on returns true
advisory.finding: apply_quota runs `xfs_quota -x -c "project -s -p /var/tmp <id>"` on the root filesystem on every --install, which recursively assigns the project id across the entire /var/tmp tree. Since compose-up.sh invokes vartmp-cap.sh --install on every deploy, once quota accounting is enabled this recursive setup walk repeats each deploy over a tree 'nobody planned the size of'.
scenarios: After the operator enables rootflags=pquota, every subsequent deploy re-runs a recursive project-id assignment over a large /var/tmp during the deploy tick.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a --install test with quota_accounting=True asserting XFS_QUOTA_LOG contains `limit -p bhard=<VAR_TMP_MAX_BYTES>` for the configured project id.
evidence: vartmp-cap.sh apply_quota(): `xfs_quota -x -c "limit -p bhard=${VAR_TMP_MAX_BYTES} ${VAR_TMP_PROJECT_ID}" "$VAR_TMP_QUOTA_FS"` runs only after `quota_accounting_on` passes
search of tests/scripts/test_vartmp_cap.py for `bhard`: (no matches)
tests/scripts/test_vartmp_cap.py:245 and :252 are the only quota_accounting=True calls, both invoking `--check-quota`, never `--install`

The fixture already records issued commands: `printf '%s\n' "$*" >> "$XFS_QUOTA_LOG"` (tests/scripts/test_vartmp_cap.py:92), so the applied `bhard=<VAR_TMP_MAX_BYTES>` command is assertable but unasserted

Named violating input: `vartmp-cap.sh --install` on a host where `xfs_quota state -p` reports Accounting: ON — a regression setting the wrong bhard value, project id, or dropping the `limit -p` call would pass all existing tests
advisory.finding: vartmp-cap.sh's newly-added apply_quota() path that actually applies the hard XFS project quota (`xfs_quota -x -c "project -s -p ... ${VAR_TMP_PROJECT_ID}"` and `"limit -p bhard=${VAR_TMP_MAX_BYTES} ..."`) is never exercised by a test. Every quota test runs with the accounting-off or enforcement-off branch; no `--install` test runs with the kernel accounting ON, so the branch that sets the real ceiling with the correct byte value and project id is uncovered.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test `test_install_applies_the_bhard_limit_when_the_kernel_is_accounting` that runs `--install` with `quota_accounting=True`, then asserts the XFS_QUOTA_LOG contains a `limit -p bhard=<cap>` line and a `project -s` line for VAR_TMP_PROJECT_ID.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the documented ~2-of-24 absence rate with treat_missing_data=breaching+2/3 on the success-gated usage metric (widen the window, or move silence-detection onto the cleanup heartbeat only).
evidence: infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf:660-669 `period = 300` / `evaluation_periods = 3` / `datapoints_to_alarm = 2` / `treat_missing_data = "breaching"`
infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf:658-659 comment: '2 breaching datapoints in a 3-period window absorbs the ordinary timer jitter that makes ~2 of 24 periods absent on this box'
observability.sh publishes var_tmp_used_percent only on a successful du (comment at monitoring_autodeploy.tf:666-668)
dropped.finding: rebar-var-tmp-usage-high uses treat_missing_data = "breaching" on var_tmp_used_percent, but that metric is published ONLY on a successful measurement and the design itself notes ~2 of 24 periods are normally absent from timer jitter. With evaluation_periods=3 / datapoints_to_alarm=2, two absent (=breaching) periods inside any 3-period window will drive the alarm to ALARM even when /var/tmp is well under budget, producing pages unrelated to usage.
scenarios: Two consecutive du timeouts / jitter within a 3-period window while usage is healthy -> ALARM fires on absence, not on high usage.
